title: Strict-diagram normalization of integral open product comparisons
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p^a}}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Use a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with its specified canonical exchange and projection transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all morphisms are separated of finite type. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite stages. Take $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$, and let $f=aj:X\to B$, $g=bk:Y\to B$ be compactifications with open $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$ and proper $a,b$. Put $T=X\times_BY$, $\bar T=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $u=j\times_Bk$, $c:\bar T\to B$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and, for a third factor, $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ with compactification $h=dl$ of $W\to B$. Use their actual strict finite reduction diagrams, whose $m$th components are derived reductions modulo $I^m$, and the completed operation comparisons of [def-exchange-projection, fix-lem-exchanges]. In the derived categories of strict diagrams of constant $\mathcal O_E$-module sheaves, write $J_v$ for termwise extension by zero along an open $v$ and $G_v$ for termwise restriction. The sheaf open base-change and projection maps with their quotient-ring actions induce diagram morphisms
$$e^\bullet_{j,k}:(J_jK_\bullet)\boxtimes^L_{A_{E,\bullet}}(J_kL_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_u(K_\bullet\boxtimes^L_{A_{E,\bullet}}L_\bullet),$$
where tensor is the derived pointwise tensor of diagrams over the quotient-ring diagram $m\mapsto A_{E,m}$ and $\boxtimes$ includes projection pullbacks. These maps restrict to the identity and satisfy the swapped-factor and three-factor associativity equalities in the derived diagram category. Under the proper/open diagram comparisons $\Gamma_Q$ of [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison], the diagram expansion of the canonical exchange/PF compactification composite equals the proper composite followed by $R_c^{\mathcal T}(e^\bullet_{j,k})$, where $R_c^{\mathcal T}$ is total derived termwise direct image. Applying functorial $R\lim$ and the completed operation comparisons yields a natural completed isomorphism
$$e^c_{j,k}:(j_!K)\boxtimes(k_!L)\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!(K\boxtimes L)$$
with the same signed symmetry and associativity equalities, and the completed compactification identity
$$\lambda_{aj,bk}(K,L)=Rc_*(e^c_{j,k})\circ\lambda_{a,b}(j_!K,k_!L).$$
Here $\lambda$ is the explicit exchange/projection composite defined in [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity], now evaluated with completed operations. The finite reductions are bounded constructible and have bounded etale-origin witnesses; only the actual reduction diagrams carry transitions, and no transitions between the witnesses are assumed. Rationalization of these morphisms, and scalar extension from a common finite coefficient field to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, yield the same open comparison identities and compactification identity in those stages. No faithfulness of finite reduction on integral derived morphisms is asserted.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_m=R/\varpi_E^m$. The valuation ring is a DVR with finite residue field, hence is Noetherian, and each $A_m$ is finite. Finite-type schemes over the field $k$ are Noetherian. All opens in question are quasi-compact since their source schemes are Noetherian. Base change and composition of proper morphisms show that the proper projections and the product structural map $c$ used below are proper. These check the coefficient, scheme and properness hypotheses of the tower proper/open comparison; they do not impose any additional condition on the compactifications. Completeness of $E$ also gives $R\cong\lim_m R/\varpi_E^m$: representatives of compatible residue classes are Cauchy since successive differences lie in $\varpi_E^mR$; their limit has absolute value at most one and represents every residue class. Injectivity follows since $|\varpi_E|^m\to0$. Thus $\varpi_E$ is a non-zero-divisor and the complete-ring hypothesis of the coefficient-system comparison is satisfied.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; diagram-site application and explicit adjunction calculation

proof.text: Work first in $D(\mathscr S_Z)$, where $\mathscr S_Z$ is the abelian category of strict semilinear $(A_m)_Z$-module systems. The actual reductions of $K,L,M$ are objects of this category, not independently chosen derived levels. Use its simultaneous system pullbacks $P_v$, right adjoints $S_v$, derived tensor, and exact $J_j\dashv P_j$. The system comparison theorem supplies their evaluations, units, counits and quotient compatibility. The simultaneous section model supplies the projection and exchange maps as actual counit mates. At the end forget the ring-system action to obtain maps in the derived categories of constant-$R$ towers. This direction only applies a functor to equalities; it never infers an equality from forgotten or evaluated maps. Tensor throughout this construction is over the ring system $(A_m)_m$, not the tensor of the forgotten $R$-module towers.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); simultaneous system models are the assertions of the two cited DAG nodes

proof.text: Factor $u=j_1k_1$ through $X\times_B\bar Y$, where $j_1$ is the base change of $j$ and $k_1$ the base change of $k$. Apply the diagram-site maps $\beta,\gamma$ of open-tensor normalization: first replace $P_{\bar p}J_jK_\bullet$ by $J_{j_1}P K_\bullet$; move the other tensor factor inside $J_{j_1}$ by $\gamma_{j_1}$; replace its restricted $k$-extension by $J_{k_1}q^*L_\bullet$; move this extension outside the inner tensor using signed symmetry and $\gamma_{k_1}$; finally compose open extensions. Every arrow is an isomorphism. Their composite is $e^\bullet_{j,k}$. Each $\beta,\gamma$ restricts to the identity under the open units, so $P_u e^\bullet_{j,k}=1_{K_\bullet\boxtimes L_\bullet}$. All arrows were formed over $(A_m)_m$, so in particular they preserve quotient actions and transitions.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), with sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I; normalized ringed diagram-site maps of the cited node

proof.text: The opposite factorization gives a second map between the same objects, both of which the preceding construction identifies with $J_u(K_\bullet\boxtimes L_\bullet)$. Full faithfulness of $J_u$ implies that restriction to $u$ is injective on the Hom set between these objects. Both restrictions are the identity, hence the two maps agree. For a swap, compare $e^\bullet_{k,j}\sigma$ with $J_u(\sigma)e^\bullet_{j,k}$ after identifying the swapped product schemes. Their restrictions are the same signed symmetry. For three factors both iterated maps have objects in the essential image of the total open extension; their restrictions are the canonical tensor associator. The same injectivity proves the signed symmetry and associativity equalities in the derived system category itself.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; diagram-site application and explicit adjunction calculation

proof.text: For the compactification calculation, use instead the factorization through $V=\bar X\times_B Y$. Write $i:V\hookrightarrow\bar T$, $v:T\hookrightarrow V$, $r:V\to Y$, $s:V\to\bar X$ and $z:\bar T\to\bar Y$ for its maps, so $u=iv$, $zi=kr$, and $r,z$ are proper. Put $F=S_aJ_jK_\bullet$, $H=P_bF$, $N=J_kL_\bullet$, $V_0=P_{\bar p}J_jK_\bullet$ and $E=\operatorname{Ex}_{a,b}(J_jK_\bullet):H\to S_zV_0$. Set $D=K_\bullet\boxtimes L_\bullet$. Denote by $\tau:(P_iV_0)\otimes P_rL_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}J_vD$ the open base-change and tensor comparison. The $k$-first factorization in Step 3 gives $e^\bullet$ as $V_0\otimes P_zJ_kL_\bullet\to J_i((P_iV_0)\otimes P_rL_\bullet)\xrightarrow{J_i\tau}J_iJ_vD$. Let $\lambda_Q:P_kS_zJ_i\cong S_r$ and $\Gamma_Q:J_kS_r\to S_zJ_i$ be the normalized proper/open maps for this square.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; diagram-site application and explicit adjunction calculation

proof.text:
Let $B_z:P_kS_z\xrightarrow{\sim}S_rP_i$ be open restriction of direct image in this square. Its normalization on $J_i$ is $\lambda_Q$. Pullback pasting for the two squares defining $E$ and $B_z$ gives
$$B_z\,P_kE=\operatorname{Ex}_{a,bk}(J_jK_\bullet):P_kH\longrightarrow S_rP_iV_0.$$
This is the mate-pasting equation: the right-side pullback square is the composite of the square over $b$ and the square over $k$. Its counit is the pasted counit, so the canonical compositors are those in the left side. The open base-change identification $P_iV_0\cong J_vP_pK_\bullet$ then gives precisely the exchange for $aj$ along $bk$ before its compact-support notation is applied. These are identities of ringed diagram-site adjunctions, not conclusions from their finite evaluations.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); explicit pasting of the square over b with its restriction over k

proof.text:
Write $\pi_z$ and $\pi_r$ for counit-defined ordinary projection maps. The proper/open tensor equality, or equivalently its open-adjunction transpose, gives
$$S_z(e^\bullet)\,\pi_z(E\otimes1_N)
=\Gamma_{Q,J_vD}\,J_k\!\left(S_r\tau\,\pi_r((B_zP_kE)\otimes1_L)\right)\,\gamma'_k.$$
Here $\gamma'_k:H\otimes J_kL\to J_k(P_kH\otimes L)$ is the open tensor comparison with its signed symmetry. To see the equality, first precompose both sides with $(\gamma'_k)^{-1}$ and transpose under $J_k\dashv P_k$. On the right $\lambda_Q P_k\Gamma_Q=1$ leaves $S_r\tau\,\pi_r((B_zP_kE)\otimes1)$. On the left the exchange/tensor compatibility square for $z$ restricted along $k$ replaces $P_k\pi_z$ by $\pi_r(B_z\otimes1)$; the normalized open maps restrict to identities and give exactly that same expression. Thus equality follows from injectivity of the adjunction bijection, with no claim that $P_k$ is faithful on arbitrary Hom sets.

source.place: Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram); open-adjunction transpose calculation using the normalized proper/open map

proof.text: Expand the left compact-support expression using $aj$, $bk$ and $q=rv$. By definition its exchange is the map identified in Step 6. Its projection for $q$ is $S_r(\gamma_v)\pi_r$, so the middle exchange/projection expression is $S_r\tau\,\pi_r((B_zP_kE)\otimes1)$. Its projection for $bk$ first applies the projection for $b$ and then $S_b\gamma'_k$, after the two specified symmetries. Finally composition across the proper/open square $zi=kr$ applies $S_b\Gamma_Q$, with target $S_bS_zJ_uD$. The system composition comparison uses exactly this normalized $\Gamma_Q$, by the horizontal and vertical pasting laws. Consequently the right-hand expression of Step 7, after $S_b$ and this initial projection for $b$, is the actual diagram expansion of $\lambda_{aj,bk}$. The left-hand expression is $S_bS_z(e^\bullet)\lambda_{a,b}(J_jK_\bullet,J_kL_\bullet)$. The direct-image compositor identifies $S_bS_z$ with $S_c$, proving the asserted diagram compactification identity.

proof.text:
Check the realization domain rather than adding transitions to the supplied witnesses. The integral finite-Tor definition gives common Tor intervals for all reductions. Finite pullback preserves these intervals, tensor adds them, and open extension preserves both the cohomological and Tor intervals. Bounded constructible reductions have bounded etale origin. If coherent etale models are needed for realization, apply $R
u_{A,*}$ to the actual bounded-below system: the coefficient-system comparison gives an invertible counit $
u_A^*R
u_{A,*}N	o N$, since each evaluation has etale origin. It also preserves normalization. This constructs a coherent origin presentation from the actual system; it assumes no transitions between the initially supplied witnesses. Thus all open and tensor expressions of Steps 3--4 are normalized with common finite bounds.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0941; bounds and origin checks from the cited finite coefficient and system comparison statements

proof.text: The same check applies to the proper expressions in Steps 5--8. There are only finitely many source schemes. Each has finite dimension; choose a finite dimension bound $d$ for each, taking $d=0$ for an empty source. The etale direct-image vanishing bound $2d$ works for every $A_m$, independently of $m$. The direct-image Tor-amplitude theorem therefore sends an interval $[a,b]$ to $[a,b+2d]$, preserving constructibility. Transport these finite images through the etale-origin comparison and the evaluated system adjunctions. The operation/reduction comparisons preserve the normalized transitions. Repeating for the finitely many proper factors gives common cohomological and Tor intervals for all intermediate expressions. No unbounded collection of dimension bounds or uniform choice of etale witnesses is involved.

source.place: Tag 0941; finite dimension, uniform vanishing and finite-Tor checks supplied by the cited DAG statements

proof.text:
Apply the functorial total limit to the actual system map $e^\bullet$ and the equalities of Steps 4 and 8, using termwise scalar restriction. The realization comparisons $c_V$ intertwine open maps, tensor/pullback, adjunction units and counits, proper/open interchange and all their whiskerings. Their hypotheses were checked in Steps 9--10. They therefore identify the limit of $e^\bullet$ with a specified natural map
$$e^c_{j,k}:(j_!K)\boxtimes(k_!L)\longrightarrow u_!(K\boxtimes L).$$
A functor preserves isomorphisms and equalities, hence $e^c$ is invertible and satisfies the same signed symmetry and associativity equations. The comparison for the proper/open generator is the one whose constant-$R$ tower version is $\Gamma_Q$ in the item: both are adjunct to the inverse normalized open restriction. Its finite evaluations are the canonical proper/open maps on each bounded etale-origin input. Thus the diagram identity already proved uses exactly the comparisons required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); total-limit functor and generator-intertwining realization comparisons of the cited nodes

proof.text:
Under the same realization comparisons, the limit of the diagram expansion of $\lambda$ is its completed exchange/projection definition: each factor is a canonical unit, counit, open map, tensor identification, composition comparison or a whiskering of one. The factor-intertwining property therefore identifies their ordered composite, not just its endpoints. Applying it to Step 8 gives
$$\lambda_{aj,bk}(K,L)=Rc_*(e^c_{j,k})\circ\lambda_{a,b}(j_!K,k_!L).$$
The definition in [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity] fixes the order of these factors; its finite-coefficient theorem is not being used to lift an equality. At no point is equality of integral maps deduced from equality of all finite reductions.

source.place: Tag 0941; applying a functor to the system identity of Step 8 and its specified generator comparisons

proof.text: Rationalize the integral maps and equations. The operation comparisons commute with rationalization and preserve the tensor associators, evaluations, units and counits, so the resulting maps are the prescribed $E$-coefficient open and compactification maps. For algebraically closed coefficients represent the finite list of objects and maps over a common finite coefficient field, apply its scalar-extension functor, and take their class in the common-stage category. The coefficient comparisons preserve the same canonical generators and their composition, and successive field extensions obey the cocycle stipulated in the exchange definition. Functoriality preserves all the equations, including the signed symmetry and three-factor associativity, and makes them independent of enlarging the common finite field. There is no finite-reduction functor used on field coefficients.
